claims.statement: The browser sends an Ask question by appending the user message to a per-thread local agent and calling copilotkit.runAgent against the backend graph sangam_agent; CopilotKitProvider targets /api/copilotkit and attaches the Supabase access token as an Authorization Bearer header (omitted without a token), or Bearer dev:<email> in the local DEV_LOGIN mode.

The Next.js route /api/copilotkit is a thin CopilotKit runtime that maps sangam_agent to an HttpAgent on AGENT_URL (default http://localhost:8000/agent) and sangam_ingest and sangam_proposal to the sibling /ingest and /proposal URLs, with maxDuration 1800; it holds no auth or SQL logic.

AuthMiddleware resolves the caller once per request as plain ASGI so chat streaming is not buffered; with SUPABASE_URL unset every request is the dev user (Bearer dev:<email> selects a seeded @local.test user under DEV_AUTH), otherwise no header is anonymous, a valid Supabase JWT is that user, Bearer dev works only with DEV_AUTH, and anything else is 401; it also records the caller's Postgres role (anon or authenticated) and claims on the request state.

ask_access (the dependency on /agent; /ingest uses require_scout plus chat_access and /proposal uses proposal_chat_access) requires a signed-in principal, claims the thread for new thread ids, returns 404 for a thread owned by someone else with no staff exemption, sets the chat_user_id and chat_scope context variables for tools and tracing, and sets agent_caller so Ask SQL runs as the caller.

The agent graphs are built lazily on the first request that needs one, under an asyncio lock, and each request clones the SessionScopedAGUIAgent because LangGraphAgent keeps per-run state on the instance; the response streams AG-UI events through an EventEncoder.

At boot the lifespan opens the shared psycopg pool, refuses to start if the SQL catalog allowlist disagrees with the database schema, opens the Postgres checkpointer on the same pool and registers /agent and /ingest routes.

build_agent creates a deep agent with six tools (db_list_tables, db_describe_table, db_profile_column, db_query, search_graph, compare_fit; fetch_url is gone) plus read_file and ls skill readers and the Postgres checkpointer. The middleware list it passes is, in order: skill-reading filesystem tools, tool_errors, sql_retry_limiter, model_call_cap, CompareFitBudget, context clearing, an optional ModelFallbackMiddleware, cheap_summarizer, and answer_audit appended only when sql_audit_model is non-empty. The graph is bound to a recursion_limit (default 200) and the Langfuse trace config.

Conversation state is checkpointed to Postgres on every graph step keyed by thread id, so a follow-up resumes from the saved messages and a reopened chat is rebuilt from graph state after an ownership check (can_open), returning 404 if the caller may not open it.

db_query validates model-written SQL with sqlglot and executes only the regenerated statement; the validator rejects non-single-query input, writes, recursive CTEs, unknown tables or columns, cross-schema references, disallowed functions and placeholders, expands star while dropping heavy columns, adds provenance columns, and clamps or injects a LIMIT.

The SQL executor runs each query in a read-only transaction with statement_timeout (default 5,000 ms), a 1 s lock timeout and a 10 s idle-in-transaction timeout, using a prepared statement so the server refuses multi-statement input, under a semaphore sized below the pool (pool size minus 3, minimum 2) so the checkpointer is not starved.

The row cap defaults to 50 (sql_max_rows) with a hard validator maximum of 200; the validator requests one extra row to detect truncation, and a truncated result tells the model it is not a complete picture and must not be presented as totals, without counting as a failed attempt. Rendering also caps cells at 200 characters and the grid at 6,000 characters.

Validator rejections reach the model as 'db_query rejected: ...' strings (including 'the query could not be checked' for a validator crash), and database errors as a multi-line 'db_query failed: Postgres <sqlstate>.' message holding the primary server message, an optional HINT, an 'executed:' line, table columns for some SQLSTATEs, a SQLSTATE-specific 'Next:' step (a 5 s timeout is 57014 with advice to narrow or aggregate), capped at 1,500 characters. Connection-level errors (no SQLSTATE) return a generic 'database is unreachable' message that omits driver text (it can contain the DSN) and tells the model not to retry.

sql_retry_limiter ends a turn after 5 failed SQL calls since the user's latest message by appending a fixed give-up AI message and jumping to the end of the graph. It counts tool results of db_query and db_profile_column that start with their rejected or failed prefixes (the COUNTED map), uses the MAX_SQL_ATTEMPTS constant (which a test pins against the prompt), and does not read the sql_max_attempts setting; db_list_tables and db_describe_table are not counted.

db_query results carry citation markers like [org:12] on rows only when the table's id (or foreign-key) column is projected, driven by catalog CITE_COLUMNS, plus a deduped sources: block (at most 8 entries) and an executed: line; the sources grammar is a contract parsed by the frontend.

The browser rebuilds each Turn from the AG-UI message stream, joining tool calls to tool results by toolCallId and treating non-subagent assistant text as the answer; AnswerCard rewrites [kind:id] markers into sangam:// links rendered as CitationChips, which link to the Registry for org, funder and score, link for activity only when the registry index holds the partner line, and render unlinked for grant, news and graph.

The answer audit runs as an after_agent hook only when sql_audit_model is set (default anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5, 'off' disables it); it is skipped when no SQL ran or no answer exists, checks grain, filters, false zeros and numbers with a cheap model, and on a warn appends the caveat as a second AIMessage prefixed with a warning sign.

The answer audit never blocks or rewrites a turn: any audit failure, unparseable reply or unresolvable model is logged and the turn continues unaudited, a warn without a caveat is ignored, and the caveat message is skipped by collect_turn so it is never mistaken for the answer; every audited turn is scored on the trace (1.0 ok, 0.0 warn).

Langfuse tracing is attached to the graph via trace_config with the masking hook registered before the graph is built; SessionScopedAGUIAgent tags each run with the thread id as session, the user id and the AG-UI run id, flushes traces in a finally block after the stream ends, and tracing failures degrade to untraced rather than breaking the turn.

Trace payloads are clipped to 4,000 characters, and with LANGFUSE_MASK_TOOL_RESULTS on the row data below the columns: line is replaced by a redaction stub while the query, executed line and sources survive; SQL statements are recorded as retriever spans with row counts, and a cancelled turn (client disconnect) is ended as cancelled rather than as an error.

db_query runs on the application's shared owner pool, but each query's transaction is read-only and switches via set_caller to the caller's anon or authenticated role and claims (from agent_caller, anon if unset), so RLS applies in addition to the catalog allowlist and validator; the validator comment still records the connecting role as a superuser until a reader role lands and sql_reader_role survives only as a config comment.

Context clearing is a SteppedClearToolUsesEdit that does nothing below 60,000 tokens and past it reclaims ceil(over/20,000)*20,000 tokens from the oldest tool results, always keeping the 5 most recent and never clearing compare_fit; because it runs on a copy before each model call, what is sent stays under the trigger and the cleared set (and cached prompt prefix) moves once per step rather than on every call, unlike the earlier 40,000-token setting. Ask, Sangam Pitch and Sangam Import share clear_old_tool_results().

compare_fit(org_id) replies as text with up to 10 strong or medium fits in full (FULL_DETAIL_MAX) and every other funder on one line, with funder_ids giving any of them in full, so it stays under deepagents' 20k-token tool-result eviction. fetch_url has been removed from Ask, while the milestone 3 items of the ask-efficiency draft (automatic citation id column, prompt table map) are not in the code.

model_call_cap ends an Ask question after ask_model_call_limit model calls (default 25) since the user's latest message by appending a fixed 'ask a narrower question' message and jumping to the end, so a runaway turn stops long before recursion_limit; the jump edge reaches __end__ or an after_agent hook such as the audit.

CompareFitBudget refuses in code, with an error ToolMessage and without running the tool, a compare_fit call whose arguments (org_id and sorted funder_ids) repeat an earlier call this turn or that would be the fourth (MAX_COMPARE_FIT_CALLS is 3); a new user message resets the count and a call adding funder_ids counts as different arguments.

Ask has backstops for tool and model failure in its middleware stack: ToolErrorMiddleware (tool_errors, exactly one in Ask) turns a tool that raises into an error reply carrying only the exception type, never its message, while a GraphInterrupt still passes through; ModelFallbackMiddleware retries on RESEARCH_MODEL unless it equals MODEL; and cheap_summarizer writes summaries on UTILITY_MODEL with the agent's own thresholds.
